headline: Energy Leads as September Opens Under Pressure; Breadth Leans Bearish
body_html:
Tuesday's session is shaping up as a bruising start to what has historically been the calendar's most unforgiving month. Mid-session breadth confirms the defensive tone: 344 names in our universe are trading lower against just 201 gainers, and the sector map is a study in rotation away from rate-sensitive and consumer-facing names. Homebuilders are the day's worst-performing pocket, off 1.79%, with Consumer and Materials not far behind. The backdrop is unmistakable — the 10-year Treasury yield has climbed to its highest level since January 2025, with fresh Middle East tensions pushing oil prices up and mortgage rates to a peak not seen since June of last year.

Against that drag, Energy stands alone in meaningful positive territory, up 1.2% as Schlumberger adds nearly 5% and oilfield-services names broadly benefit from the crude rally tied to ongoing conflict near Iran's key export infrastructure. Semiconductors are also quietly green, rising 0.73%, lifted by strong individual movers even as Software treads water just below the flat line.

The standout mover of the session is Roblox, surging more than 7%, while CrowdStrike adds 5.77% and Tesla tacks on 5.5%. Heading into the close, all eyes remain on Treasury yields and any further geopolitical developments that could extend the oil bid or deepen the pressure on rate-sensitive sectors.

briefs.headline: Yields Spike to 17-Month High on Middle East Flare-Up
briefs.body: The 10-year Treasury yield has reached its highest point since January 2025 as renewed hostilities in the Middle East stoke safe-haven flows into oil and out of risk assets. The move is rippling through mortgage markets, where rates have simultaneously vaulted to their loftiest reading since June 2025, adding fresh headwinds to an already strained housing sector.

briefs.headline: Roblox Surges More Than 7%, Pacing All Gainers Mid-Session
briefs.body: Roblox is the clear standout in today's otherwise cautious tape, jumping 7.16% to lead every name in our universe through the midday hour. The internet-gaming platform's rally is bucking broad consumer weakness and drawing attention as one of the few high-beta growth names finding aggressive buyers on the session's opening day of September.

briefs.headline: Citadel Warns Seasonal and Valuation Headwinds Are Converging
briefs.body: Strategists at Citadel flagged that the risk-reward calculus for equities is deteriorating just as the market enters its historically weakest stretch of the year. The caution lands on a day when negative breadth already outpaces positive breadth by a ratio of roughly 1.7-to-1 across our tracked universe, lending early data support to the concern.

briefs.headline: White House Said to Near Drug-Pricing Deals With Multiple Manufacturers
briefs.body: Reports indicate the Trump administration is preparing to announce negotiated pharmaceutical pricing arrangements with close to a dozen drugmakers. The development follows Eli Lilly's separate move to deploy obesity-drug revenues toward additional acquisitions, suggesting dealmaking and policy pressure are colliding simultaneously across the healthcare landscape.

briefs.headline: Oil Infrastructure Fears Fuel Energy-Services Rally; SLB Climbs Nearly 5%
briefs.body: Schlumberger advanced 4.83% mid-session as analysts and investors focused on the vulnerability of Iranian export facilities following geopolitical signals from Washington. Energy is the only sector in our universe posting a gain above 1% on the day, with the oilfield-services segment absorbing a disproportionate share of the sector's inflows.

briefs.headline: Consumer and Homebuilder Names Bear the Brunt of Rate Anxiety
briefs.body: Floor & Decor, Gap Inc., Burlington Stores, Vita Coco, and Clorox are all shedding between 4.7% and 5.2% mid-session, collectively dragging Consumer down 1.26% as a sector. Homebuilders are faring even worse at minus 1.79%, a direct reflection of surging mortgage rates that are squeezing affordability expectations well into next year.
